clue.text: Some pretty Baltic prince with a short fuse

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered prince from somewhere attractive on the Baltic coast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet this hothead is mocked as 'Prince of Cats', so 'prince' is fair for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's quarrelsome cousin is called Prince of Cats by Mercutio and is quick to anger and draw his sword.

clue.text: Dried-up grass flipping loves one into The Stones

indicators.note: flipping means the dried grass word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried for fodder
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like the letter O, so two loves give OO

explanation.surface: A dried-up old fan of the Rolling Stones gets carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stones' suggests the rock band, but in Gulliver's Travels these brutish creatures are obsessed with digging up and hoarding shining stones.
explanation.definitionFit: In Swift's Book IV the brutes of Houyhnhnm-land prize glittering stones above all, so each is literally keen on stones.

clue.text: A large fish and cut of pork for Campion's producer

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family
ham is the cured cut from a pig's hind leg

explanation.surface: Ordering seafood and a pork joint to feed a camping party.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Campion is the gentleman sleuth created by the crime writer Margery Allingham, so his 'producer' is his author.
explanation.definitionFit: Margery of that surname wrote the detective novels featuring Albert Campion, so she created him.

clue.text: Pickwickian place sent up by masculine article

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to place something is to put it
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A spot satirised by some male-written essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracy of that name is one of the members of the Pickwick Club in Dickens's Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: See you possibly bypass house-swapping work

parts.note: ta-ra is an informal British goodbye, much like see you
a bypass is a road skirting round a town

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye as you take the ring road round the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Maeve Binchy's novel Tara Road follows two women who swap houses between Dublin and Connecticut.
explanation.definitionFit: Maeve Binchy's novel is built on two women exchanging homes across the Atlantic, so it is a work about a house swap.

clue.text: Where moths go at night and shelter is novel

parts.note: moths are drawn towards a lamp or flame after dark
a house is a shelter or dwelling

explanation.surface: A nature note on where moths fly after dark, followed by a remark that a refuge is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition: Virginia Woolf's 1927 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's 1927 book about the Ramsay family is a famous modernist novel.

clue.text: One impersonating a shepherd or lords in a comic

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters are played around with for laughs, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone playing a shepherd, or perhaps some aristocrats, in a funny paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a comic' looks like 'in a magazine', but 'in a' is part of the fodder and 'comic' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It the heroine disguises herself as the youth Ganymede and lives as a shepherd in the Forest of Arden.

clue.text: Soldiers and a bishop receiving hard drug treatment

indicators.note: receiving means the group of letters takes in the next piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps, so soldiers
B is the chess notation for bishop
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Troops and a cleric taking in a hard drug, by way of some medication.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation is the course of therapy that helps addicts come off substances.

clue.text: "May we cram / Within this wooden O the very casques / That did affright the air at —?" (Shakespeare)

definitions.text: "May we cram / Within this wooden O the very casques / That did affright the air at —?" (Shakespeare)

parts.words: "May we cram / Within this wooden O the very casques / That did affright the air at —?" (Shakespeare)
parts.note: the Chorus in the Prologue to Henry V asks whether the theatre can hold the helmets of Henry's famous 1415 battle against the French

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Prologue to Henry V with its final word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'wooden O' is the round Globe theatre; the missing word is the battlefield where Henry V defeated the French in 1415.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chorus names the battle of 1415 in northern France where English archers routed the French.

clue.text: Load loads picked up for Yellow Sands architect

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: to load is to fill, and loads are pots, as in pots of money

explanation.surface: A labourer piling up heavy cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden Phillpotts co-wrote the comedy Yellow Sands, so 'architect' means its author.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden of that name wrote the play Yellow Sands with his daughter Adelaide, so he built it.

clue.text: Musical broadcast after premier of Hamilton

indicators.note: after means the broadcast word is placed following the letter before it
the premier of something is its first, so this takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A show transmitted after the opening night of the hit musical Hamilton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a misspelt 'premiere', fitting a musical, but it means first.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s rock musical about hippies and the Vietnam draft is named after the long locks of its tribe.

clue.text: Show some cheek and mug tree-dweller

parts.note: to moon is to bare one's buttocks, literally showing some cheek
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: Being cheeky and pulling a face at an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonface is a character living at the top of Enid Blyton's Faraway Tree, a classic British children's series.
explanation.definitionFit: In Enid Blyton's Faraway Tree books the round-faced character lives in a room at the very top of the tree.

clue.text: Live in Providence where the Buddenbrooks live

indicators.note: in means the living word goes inside the providence word

parts.note: providence in the sense of fortune is luck
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Settling in Providence, Rhode Island, home to a famous family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providence' looks like the American city, but it means fortune; Thomas Mann's Buddenbrooks family are merchants in the German port.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann set his novel Buddenbrooks in his home city, the Hanseatic port on the Baltic.

clue.text: Knight seen with Cinders is a funny versifier

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
ash is what is left of burnt coal, cinders

explanation.surface: A knight escorting Cinderella to the ball proves a comic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cinders' is the nickname for Cinderella, but here it means burnt remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogden of that surname was an American writer of humorous light verse.

clue.text: "Peace is an — in a war that is continuously going on" (Thucydides)

definitions.text: "Peace is an — in a war that is continuously going on" (Thucydides)

parts.words: "Peace is an — in a war that is continuously going on" (Thucydides)
parts.note: the Greek historian of the Peloponnesian War calls peace merely a pause agreed in fighting that never truly ends

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Greek historian Thucydides with one word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is a truce, a halt in fighting agreed by both sides.

clue.text: Reilly was one dressed in a suit around Gulf

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
dressed suggests the letters are arranged or prepared differently, so they are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for gulf on maps

explanation.surface: Someone called Reilly wore a suit somewhere around the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the anagram of INASUIT round G. Ignatius J. Reilly is the hero of John Kennedy Toole's A Confederacy of Dunces.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of A Confederacy of Dunces bears that first name, so Reilly was one by name.

clue.text: Adventurous lad is warm, yet so in need of correction

indicators.note: letters in need of correction are in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a boy is affectionate but still needs disciplining.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy hero gets into scrapes and has many escapades along the Mississippi.

clue.text: Possibilities author initially rejected to block-up nasty sink

indicators.note: to block up a gap is to fill it, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: nasty means bad

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: to sink a post or object in the ground is to bury it

explanation.surface: An author first rejected the idea of unblocking a horrid sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Malcolm Bradbury wrote Possibilities, a 1973 book of essays on the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm of that surname published the critical essays Possibilities, so he is its author.

clue.text: In a month, one's to see a spoilt little woman

indicators.note: In means the possessive word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: March is the third month
one's, the possessive, means my when speaking of oneself

explanation.surface: Within a month, someone will see a pampered small lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' hides Little Women: the youngest March sister in Louisa May Alcott's novel is vain and indulged.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest sister in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women is pampered and vain, so she is a spoilt little woman.

clue.text: Part of barmy theory that's not true

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Dismissing a bit of a crackpot idea as false.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable or falsehood is something untrue, so the definition is a phrase describing it.

clue.text: Publicity published about southern writer of The Fugitive

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity

indicators.note: about means the published word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a book that is out is published

explanation.surface: Promotion for a book released about a Southern writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fugitive is the English title of Albertine disparue, a volume of In Search of Lost Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel of that name wrote Albertine disparue, translated as The Fugitive, part of his great novel sequence.

clue.text: Old laws broken by Duke, a scheming character in Shakespeare

indicators.note: broken laws are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A duke breaks ancient laws, a plotting figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril's steward in King Lear is a servile schemer who carries her plots.

clue.text: A bribe intercepted by head of Europol for fabulist

indicators.note: intercepted by means another piece cuts into the middle of these letters

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A bribe caught by the European police chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of Europol' looks like the agency's director, but it is its first letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is known for moral fables with animal characters.

clue.text: Hand-rear bats for one who wrote of Hilda Stafford

definitions.text: one who wrote of Hilda Stafford

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bringing up baby bats by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Beatrice Harraden wrote Hilda Stafford, a novel of the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice of that name, a Victorian novelist, wrote the novel Hilda Stafford.

clue.text: Best bud of Bert Berns essentially one on drug

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits on top of the next
essentially means the essence or core of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Songwriter Bert Berns at heart was a man on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bert Berns was an American songwriter; the definition is Bert's Sesame Street friend.
explanation.definitionFit: On Sesame Street the muppet pair share a flat and are inseparable friends.

clue.text: Poor imperial goons serving leaders Napoleon and Minimus?

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Poor imperial thugs in service to two rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon and Minimus are characters in Orwell's Animal Farm; the question mark marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: In Orwell's Animal Farm the dictator and the poet are both swine.

clue.text: A US guru upset with any compatriots of Eduardo Galeano

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American spiritual teacher is upset, as is anybody from his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Eduardo Galeano was a writer from Montevideo, so his fellow countrymen are from that South American nation.

clue.text: They open up for New Order member

indicators.note: up means messed up or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fans of the band New Order unlock the doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Order' looks like the band, but it means a member newly admitted to a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a newly admitted member of a religious community, a convert or beginner.

clue.text: Poetic type offensive about queen going to Cuba

indicators.note: about means the offensive word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of 1968 was a major Vietnam War campaign
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: An offensive is launched against a queen sailing to Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective describing a rude poem, but it is the noun: the Tet Offensive of the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line stanza is a verse form, a kind of poetic unit.
